results.title: Mexico predicted lineup for FIFA World Cup 2026 ft. Guillermo Ochoa & Raúl Jiménez
highlights:
## Mexico are in Group G of the FIFA World Cup 2026.
[...]
The weight of home expectations will be used to evaluate Mexico’s FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign. Normally, it would be obvious to aim for the top spot in a group that includes South Africa, the Korean Republic, and the Czech Republic.
[...]
The team has been assembled across several generations. While Alvarez, Jimenez, and Cesar Montes provide the club with experience, Ochoa’s presence is meaningful.
[...]
Armando Gonzalez, Brian Gutierrez, Obed Vargas, and Gilberto Mora provide freshness on the other end. Julian Quinones provides Mexico with physicality and direct running, while Santiago Gimenez provides a penalty-box striker.
[...]
### Mexico predicted lineup: 4-2-3-1
[...]
#### GK: Guillermo Ochoa
[...]
Guillermo Ochoa is set to make history at the World Cup when he starts for the co-host nation and makes his sixth World Cup appearance. No Mexican goalie has more experience than Ochoa at the World Cup, having been their starting goalkeeper at every World Cup. Hence, we can expect him to be in the starting lineup in their opening game.
[...]
#### RB: Jorge Sánchez
[...]
Jorge Sanchez will lead Mexico’s heart of defence as the centre-back will be counted on by the head coach to take charge of defence alongside Cesar Montes as Mexico will be hoping to prevail in their opening World Cup match in their bid to reach the knockout stage.
[...]
#### CB: César Montes
[...]
#### CB: Johan Vasquez
[...]
#### LB: Jesus Gallardo
[...]
Tell Mexico fans that one of the few holdovers from the 2018 World Cup would be Gallardo. Two things have allowed him to keep his place. First, no one has been good enough to replace him. Mateo Chavez’s charge is likely arriving too late in the cycle to displace the experienced defender from the XI.
[...]
#### DM: Edson Alvarez
[...]
The 28-year-old continues to play a crucial role in the Mexico XI. Alvarez should always be on the pitch, but Aguirre isn’t always sure where to put him. He can drop in the middle of the pitch and the centre-backs to create a three-man look, and he is occasionally used as a centre-back.
